title: On the Relationship Between the Developer's Perceptible Race and Ethnicity and the Evaluation of Contributions in OSS
benchmark_measurement: Not applicable. The paper studies the relationship between developers' perceptible race/ethnicity and the evaluation of their contributions in Open Source Software (OSS). It does not measure any aspect of faith or religion.
findings: Not applicable. The paper's findings are related to race and ethnicity, not religion. It found that perceptible Non-White developers are underrepresented in OSS, and their contributions have lower odds of being accepted compared to perceptible White developers. It also found that pull requests from perceptible non-white submitters are more likely to be accepted when the integrator is from the same perceptible race/ethnicity.
